findings.result: The supplied patch adds four calls inside PANEL and one appended helper. The existing arithmetic statements, interpolation constants, R1/R2/R3 assignments, radiation weighting, and output statements are unmodified in the patch.
Stage 1 is before R3→R2; stage 2 follows R3→R2 and precedes R2→R1; stage 3 follows R2→R1 and precedes the JRAD=0 RADFNI weighting; stage 4 follows that weighting and precedes BUFOUT/PNLINT.

The helper reproduces FILHDR, SUB1, and XPANEL common-block member order from HIRAC1/PANEL, and its R1/R2/R3 arguments are INTENT(IN). Under stock linuxGNUdbl flags in the pinned build log (-fdefault-integer-8 -fdefault-real-8 -fdefault-double-8 -frecord-marker=4), default INTEGER and REAL are 8 bytes. Header payload is 8-byte tag + 19 default INTEGER values + 9 REAL*8 values; each array is emitted as its own record.

The new helper only tests layer/panel range, opens a fresh unformatted file, serializes header/arrays, and flushes. No assignment targets the caller arrays or COMMON data. Existing arithmetic expressions were not changed. This is a static review; only the required all-layer output bitwise comparison can establish runtime preservation.

The record includes V1P, DVP, NLO and the target wavenumber, enough to map the R1 grid as V1P + (i-NLO)*DVP. DVR2/DVR3 and the N1R*/N2R* indexes are included for coarse-grid reconstruction. VFT itself is omitted but is derivable from V1P and NLO under V1P=VFT+(NLO-1)*DV.

The helper uses inclusive V1P<=target<=V2P membership. A parser should group by case/layer/panel and verify exactly four ordered stage records for each intended panel; if the target lies on a shared panel boundary, duplicate panel captures must be reported rather than silently collapsed.

Retain the plan requirement to compare every layer output/header/panel sample against the corresponding existing baseline (only explicitly allowed timestamp metadata may differ), and verify the trace file separately. A successful trace build alone does not show noninterference.

open_runtime_checks: verify four stage records and stage ordering for each target and case
decode sequential record markers and confirm payload sizes against stock GNU double flags
compare complete 45-layer output files/arrays bitwise to their paired baseline
confirm any timestamp-only header exception from actual source/output contract, not by broad masking
